result: The exact SHA passes the bounded production HTTPS/restart scenario, but cannot be accepted for public deployment because the reusable launch Bearer is embedded in the public bundle and the service has only one global room.

findings.summary: The production build embeds HEXCRAWL_VTT_PREVIEW_KEY verbatim in the public editor JavaScript bundle, so the reusable Bearer value is not a server-side secret.
evidence: vite.config.ts defines __HEXCRAWL_VTT_PREVIEW_KEY__ from the environment and src/App.tsx sends it as Authorization: Bearer.
Independent sentinel build: HEXCRAWL_VTT_PREVIEW_KEY=HX078_REVIEW_SENTINEL_KEY_9dbbd6c; rg found the exact sentinel once in dist/assets/index-*.js.
scripts/vtt-preview/server.mjs accepts /open when the same Bearer is presented; Origin validation is a browser/CORS boundary, not server authentication.
findings.impact: Anyone able to download the public bundle can recover the shared launch credential and call the room creation endpoint. Rotating or hiding the build variable cannot repair this boundary.
findings.required_fix: Do not put a reusable server credential in downloadable assets. Define a production room-creation/auth boundary with server-issued/per-room authority and server-side abuse controls; extend the existing production scenario to fail if a reusable secret appears in dist.

findings.summary: The verified room service owns one global room per process/storage file and returns 409 for a different map; no public durable multi-room deployment exists.
evidence: scripts/vtt-preview/server.mjs has one `let room` and rejects a different map digest with 409.
The CI proof uses one ephemeral process and one temporary storagePath.
The normal GitHub Pages workflow supplies no VTT server URL/key, so the published static build remains VTT-disabled.
findings.impact: The CI result proves one room can survive a process restart, but it does not yield a usable shared service for independent games or an owner-accessible test stand.
findings.required_fix: Provide a production-safe room identity/storage boundary for independent games and then validate it on a durable HTTPS stand. Hosting and publication remain separate owner decisions.

findings.summary: The new production delivery scenario is useful, but the workflow executes it only when pull_request.number == 519, so the permanent test file will not protect later changes after merge.
evidence: .github/workflows/check.yml gates the scenario and artifact on PR number 519.
The scenario's distinct value is production build plus three HTTPS origins; restart and projection details reuse coverage from vtt-room-preview.mjs.
It lacks a negative assertion that reusable credentials are absent from public assets.
findings.impact: The test can pass for this PR but silently stop being a regression guard for subsequent production/VTT changes.
findings.required_fix: Keep this one scenario and make it run for the relevant permanent CI path; extend it with negative build/secret assertions instead of adding a duplicate suite.

criteria.method: Exact production HTTPS artifact and prior native-geometry evidence.
criteria.limits: One ephemeral room is verified; no public durable service or release.

criteria.method: Room restart, same player link and restricted projection over HTTPS.
criteria.limits: A reusable key is public and the service is single-room; the delivery contract is not accepted.

test_change_summary.scenario_risk: Production packaging, three HTTPS origins, durable room restart and the same restricted player link were not covered by the local functional suite.
test_change_summary.reuse_or_new_reason: The existing local VTT suite remains the detailed behavior coverage. One new top-level scenario is useful for the distinct production delivery path; it should be extended, not duplicated, to assert that no reusable server secret is shipped in public assets.
